## Simple explanation

Computer vision is the field of enabling computers to process and make
use of images or video. Tasks include recognizing objects, locating them,
segmenting regions, and estimating motion.

## Technical explanation

Computer-vision systems transform pixel data into representations and
predictions. They may use classical image-processing methods, machine
learning, deep neural networks, or combinations of these. Inputs,
annotations, image transformations, and evaluation metrics depend on the
task.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Visual models are used in robotics, manufacturing, accessibility,
healthcare, content organization, and many other areas. Engineers must
consider image quality, distribution shift, privacy, annotation quality,
and consequences of errors in the deployment context.

## How it works

An image or video is decoded and preprocessed, then a vision model extracts
features and produces task-specific outputs. These may be class labels,
bounding boxes, segmentation masks, or other measurements. Evaluation
compares outputs with suitable reference data and operational requirements.

## Practical example

We can train an image classifier to distinguish between two objects. See [Penguin vs Ostrich with FastAI](/notebooks/B/binary-classification.ipynb).



## Common misconceptions

- A vision model may rely on background or image-source cues instead of
  the intended object.
- High performance on a benchmark does not guarantee reliability on
  different cameras, environments, or populations.
- Computer vision includes more than image classification.
